solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ring in to obstruct descent

indicators.note: the clue says the ring goes in, so the circle-shaped letter is placed inside the word for obstruct

parts.note: to obstruct something is to stop it
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a ring on a pole or post to stop something sliding down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' reads as a verb (to telephone, or to encircle) but is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoop is a swoop downwards, especially a hawk's dive on its prey, so it is a descent.

clue.text: 5 6, they 22 down confused about following Christ beyond theosophy without a hint of sarcasm

indicators.note: the letters gathered here are muddled about and rearranged, so confused signals an anagram

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: without says a letter is taken away from the word theosophy
a hint of something is just its first trace, so the opening letter of sarcasm

explanation.surface: A grumble about some muddled theology that mixes Christianity with theosophy, said with a straight face.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition joins three other answers: 'singing Galway Bay, they were' completes the line from the Pogues' 'Fairytale of New York'. THEOSOPHY loses its S (the hint of 'sarcasm') to give THEOOPHY before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Pogues' Christmas song the lyric runs that the boys of the New York police choir were singing Galway Bay, so the cross-referenced words complete that line.

clue.text: See 2
Treatment of wise old don?

parts.note: a don teaches at a university, and U is the usual abbreviation for university
a sage is a wise old person

explanation.surface: A question about how a learned old university teacher is handled.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose reading: a wise old don is a university sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is handled or used, so it means treatment, as in rough usage of a car.

clue.text: Grass may be last of inmates released from prison

indicators.note: something released from the prison name leaves it, so a letter is deleted

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An informer gets out of jail as a reward for informing on the last prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S that ends 'inmates' from SING SING. Grass is British slang for an informer, or for informing; an informer who talks to the police is said to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is to inform on someone, and informing in slang is singing, so a grass may be doing exactly that.

clue.text: Where in Ireland homosexual is able to circumvent a badly-written bylaw

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go round, so the first word's letters go around the rest

parts.note: gay means homosexual

indicators.note: a badly written word has its letters jumbled, so the letters of bylaw are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gay man is clever enough to get round a sloppily drafted local rule somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is able' only joins the surface; 'badly-written' shuffles the bylaw's letters, and 'to circumvent' wraps the gay man around them and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway Bay is a large bay on the west coast of Ireland, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Rustic chap is youth personified

parts.note: a chap is a man, referred to as he
in rustic dialect is becomes be, so a country chap is 'he be'

explanation.surface: A country lad is youth itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustic' tells you to use the dialect form: a country speaker says 'he be' for 'he is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth, so she is youth in the form of a person.

clue.text: New arrangement of Messiah BBC reviews at opening of tour? A 'Fairytale' start for Shane!

indicators.note: a new arrangement puts the letters in a different order, signalling an anagram
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The BBC reviews a fresh arrangement of Handel's Messiah at the start of a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Shane MacGowan of the Pogues sang 'Fairytale of New York', whose opening line is the answer; the musical surface makes 'New arrangement' look like a description of a score.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pogues' Christmas song, sung by Shane MacGowan, opens with these words, so they are the start of that 'Fairytale'.

clue.text: "Why do I show off?" refrain

parts.note: asking why is asking what something is for
the reason for showing off is the ego, so the question is answered by self-esteem

explanation.surface: Someone asks themselves why they keep showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to the question in the clue is 'for ego'.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego (more often forgo) is to do without or abstain, which is what refrain means as a verb.

clue.text: Get to know about article from kid

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for get to know surrounds the article

parts.note: to learn something is to get to know it
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Finding out about something written by a young child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but here it is the soft leather made from young goatskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern means made of leather, and kid is a fine leather, so something made from kid is leathern.

clue.text: First under the hammer on application

parts.note: an item going under the auctioneer's hammer is a lot
I is the Roman numeral one, so first
taken as written

explanation.surface: The first item at an auction goes on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' looks like a request or the act of selling, but it means something applied to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid you apply to the skin, so it is an application in the medical sense.

clue.text: Stick the man in the middle

indicators.note: the clue puts the man in the middle, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the core is the middle of something
the man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a man the meat in the sandwich, or to put up with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like an order to place or tolerate someone, but it is the definition, meaning to cling together.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together as one, which is what things that stick do.

clue.text: Areas covered by religious officers cutting teeth at the same time, unfortunately

indicators.note: cutting means taking the word teeth away from the rearranged phrase
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

parts.note: the phrase supplies the letter pool, which holds the answer plus the letters of teeth

explanation.surface: Two clerics are both cutting teeth at once, which is bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the letters of AT THE SAME TIME, with TEETH taken out, rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the territory or office of an imam, a Muslim religious leader, so imamates are areas such officers govern.

clue.text: Take time to interrupt singly orderly line of hairdressers

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so the time letter goes inside the word singly
put in order means the letters are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A row of hairdressers taking a break from working one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take time to interrupt' puts T into SINGLY; 'orderly' then rearranges the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Styling is the business that hairdressers are in, so it is their line of work.

clue.text: Exploited menials of territorial detachment

indicators.note: exploited suggests the words are worked over, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Servants used by a breakaway territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing Crown dependency in the Irish Sea, not part of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a territory detached from Britain both geographically and politically, so it is a territorial detachment.

clue.text: Writer's no mug describing sign

indicators.note: no here means without, so the mug is taken off the writer's name

parts.note: John Steinbeck was the American author of The Grapes of Wrath
a stein is a German beer mug
describing means about or concerning, as on does in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: A judgement that some author is no fool, as shown by a signature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' reads as a fool, but it is a drinking vessel, the STEIN taken from STEINBECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to summon someone with a gesture, so it is to sign or signal to them.

clue.text: Boy's work turned over on small area, having less than one foot

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the boy's work is read backwards

parts.note: a boy is a lad
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A boy's piece of work has been flipped over onto a small patch, leaving someone short of a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the reversed LADOP after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Apodal describes animals with no feet or limbs, so they have fewer than one foot.

clue.text: Wife-beater has a belly

indicators.note: has means contains, so the wife-beater holds the letter inside him

parts.note: Mr Punch beats his wife Judy in the traditional British Punch and Judy puppet show

explanation.surface: A wife-beater with a beer gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a seaside puppet show in which Punch beats Judy.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is a large protruding stomach, so it is a belly.

clue.text: Northerly winds blowing hard, right protection for flier

indicators.note: winds means twists about, so the letters of the word are rearranged
blowing means getting rid of, so the hard and right letters are taken away

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A weather report: hard northerly winds blowing, with something about protection for a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of NORTHERLY, less H and R, rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An elytron is the hardened forewing of a beetle, which shields the delicate flight wings beneath.

clue.text: See 8
Dislike river, one providing supply to sewers

parts.note: to needle can mean to dislike or resent, a sense given in Chambers

explanation.surface: Hating the river, the supplier to the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains, but it means people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: A needler is a maker or seller of needles, so supplies people who sew.

clue.text: Faced mount to get the better of OJ?

definitions.meaning: Mount ... in South Dakota has four presidents' faces carved into it

definitions.text: to get the better of OJ?
definitions.meaning: O J Simpson was a famous American football running back, so beating him means rushing for more yards

explanation.surface: A mountain with a face, and a question of how to beat O J Simpson.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football a running back 'rushes' with the ball; O J Simpson set rushing records.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Dakota mountain carved with presidential heads is literally a mountain with faces.

clue.text: Being into women, cross literary county

indicators.note: being into means placed within, so the word for being goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a cross is drawn as the letter X
esse is Latin for being or existence

explanation.surface: Fancying women makes someone cross about a novel's setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being into women' reads as liking women; here it puts ESSE inside W and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Wessex is the region Thomas Hardy used as the setting for his novels, a county of literature.

clue.text: Used to be somewhat overpowered

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word, so the letters lie inside it

explanation.surface: Someone once dominant is now rather subdued.
explanation.definitionFit: Were is the past tense of be, so it describes what used to be the case.

clue.text: Roman battle in which Julius Caesar first appeared? I'm not sure

parts.words: in which Julius Caesar first appeared?
parts.note: Caesar first appears in Act I of Shakespeare's play Julius Caesar
um is a hesitant sound of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A history quiz question about the battle where Julius Caesar first showed up, answered hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a real battle Caesar fought; the reading is the play's first act.
explanation.definitionFit: Actium was the naval battle of 31 BC where Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Shaky's band enters chart (number 2, heading for number 1)

indicators.note: the second letter heads to first place, so it is moved to the front
enters means goes inside, so the band is placed within the chart

parts.note: a table is a chart of figures
R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: A band, nervous, enters the charts at number two and heads for the top spot.
explanation.walkthrough: REM in TABLE gives TAREMBLE; moving the second letter A to the front gives the answer. 'Number 1' looks like the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Atremble means trembling, so it describes someone or something shaky.

clue.text: Notably appropriate item hotel guest will need after night out

definitions.meaning: music in the right key is in tune, so fitting in a musical sense of notes

definitions.text: item hotel guest will need after night out
definitions.meaning: a guest returning after a night out needs the room key to get in

explanation.surface: A list item: what a hotel guest needs after a night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notably' is a pun on musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Music in key is harmonious and fitting, and the guest who has been out wants in with a key.

clue.text: Unjustly take compilers up about the demise of editor

parts.note: the compilers are us, speaking as setters

indicators.note: the word up goes about the other letters, surrounding them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the demise of a word is its end, its final letter

explanation.surface: Puzzle setters are angry about the death of their editor and seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is used twice in sense: as a word to wrap around, and in 'compilers up' meaning angry setters.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize power or position wrongfully, so it is to take unjustly.
